## Spatial & Geometric Definition
* Geometry Type: Polygon (MSU_Cell_Boundary).

* Spatial Delineation: Enclosed, impounded floodplain basin bounded by perimeter containment embankments, internal ditches, and water control structures.

* Ecological Classification: Shallow seasonally flooded palustrine emergent wetland complex.

### Primary Restoration & Engineering Objectives
* Targeted Seed & Tuber Production: Provide precise, independent hydrologic drawdowns and reflooding to stimulate high-energy forage plants (smartweeds, wild millets, sedges, sprangletop).

* Migratory Waterfowl Refueling: Provide shallow foraging water depths (2.0 to 8.0 in) timed precisely to match spring and autumn waterfowl migration pulses.

* Shorebird Staging Flats: Expose extensive mudflats during late summer (July–August) for migrating northbound and southbound shorebirds.

## Typical Cross-Sections, Dimensions & Sizing Criteria
* Cell Surface Areas: Individual management cells typically scale from 10 to 80 acres.

* Topographic Grading: Graded with gentle interior slopes (<0.1% grade) toward a central drainage swale network (bottomwidths10 to 20 ft) to ensure complete gravity drainage without water pocketing.

* Operating Depth Envelope: Maximum impounded water depth of 1.5 to 3.0 ft; drawdowns expose 100% of cell floor to atmospheric drying.

### Construction & Implementation Methodology
* Precision Earthmoving: Laser-guided bulldozers and low-ground-pressure earthmovers shaping interior swales and cell bottom micro-topography.

* Clay Liner Compaction: Where underlying alluvium contains excessive sand lenses, interior floors are sealed with a compacted 1.0- to 2.0-ft cohesive clay blanket to prevent downward water loss.

### Quality Control, Inspection & Long-Term Maintenance
* Annual Water Management Plans: Rigorous hydro-period cycling: slow spring drawdowns (March–May), summer soil drying and germination (June–August), and gradual fall re-flooding (September–November).

* Discing & Succession Setback: Rotational tractor discing or controlled burning every 3 to 5 years to reset plant succession and eliminate monotypic willow or cattail stands.

Spatial Feature Attributes
### Definition
Areas or units designed to enhance wetland habitat through the use of water containment, water supply, and water control structures.

### Purpose
The basic operating plan for a Moist Soil Management Unit (MSMU) is to keep water out in the late spring and summer and to gradually flood the area in the fall. In a multiple-cell system, independent control of water levels in each cell is preferred to allow targeted habitat management.

### Applicability
Moist Soil Management Units are typically designed to include water containment, water supply, and water control structures. Water containment is provided by construction of exterior berms, interior berms, and overflow spillways, which are used to impound water during seasonal waterfowl migrations or to keep water out of the impounded area. Water supply may be provided by either river water or groundwater through the use of a pump station or well, respectively. Water control structures are utilized to maintain desired water elevations throughout the year. (UMRR Design Handbook, 2012)

### Notes
Restoration features now have a Program_UID field to distinguish between NESP and UMRR features. Aliases without program identification will be created for any field that currently has UMRR in the name, so they can be used for NESP or UMRR data.

Attribute criteria for each field includes the following:

* Attribute Status – defines whether the field requires a value or if it is optional based on available information.
* Phases – indicates the earliest time in the project lifecycle values for this attribute are available.
* Digitizing requirements – indicates when the field value should be entered in the attribute table.

Geometry Note: No Z values are needed for this feature.

### MoistSoilMgmtUnit
(polygon) – Area or area subdivision that is managed to create moist soil units.

## Parameters

### Program_UID
Designate program NESP or UMRR.

### Project_ID (alias: PROJECT_ID)
Foreign key to the unique NESP/UMRR project ID.

### Type (alias)
A broad classification used to group NESP/UMRR restoration features into categories of similar function.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Water Level Management</td>
      <td>Measures taken to manage and manipulate water levels with the goal of improving wetland habitats.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### SubType (alias: Subtype)
A classification used to group NESP/UMRR restoration features into specific design feature categories.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Moist soil management unit</td>
      <td>Units designed to enhance wetland habitat through use of water containment, water supply, and water control structures.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Backwater lake</td>
      <td>Units designed to enhance aquatic habitat through use of water containment, water supply, and water control structures.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Cell</td>
      <td>Sub-unit of a moist soil unit, bounded by exterior and/or interior berms, allowing targeted water level management within a MSMU.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### RestorFeatStatus
A description of the status of the individual restoration. It also includes the party responsible for the individual feature.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Planned</td>
      <td>Feature is in a USACE planning stage.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Built</td>
      <td>Feature has been built by USACE. If a feature has been planned and built by USACE, once constructed, it will always be considered USACE built even if repaired under later project stages.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Enhanced</td>
      <td>The function of an existing feature not built by USACE has been enhanced by a feature that was USACE built or repaired.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Repaired</td>
      <td>An existing feature not built by USACE has been directly improved or repaired.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Planned</td>
      <td>A feature that is planned by another organization or government agency.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Built</td>
      <td>Feature has been built by another organization or government agency and is an integral part of the UMRR project.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Enhanced</td>
      <td>The function of an existing feature, built by another organization or government agency, has been enhanced by a feature that was built or repaired by a non-USACE organization or government agency.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Repaired</td>
      <td>An existing feature that has been directly improved or repaired by another organization or government agency.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### Acres
Acreage of the feature.

### Depth
Typical or design depth of the feature (e.g., target water depth), recorded in appropriate units (commonly feet).

### WaterControlType
General classification of how water control is achieved.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Passive</td>
      <td>Water control depends on natural processes (e.g., seasonal inundation) or passive engineering structures (e.g., spillway or notch).</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Active</td>
      <td>Water control depends on human actions (e.g., pump station operation, stoplog structures).</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### WaterControlMethod
Specific water control technique used.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Overflow spillway</td>
      <td>Section of embankment engineered to provide controlled overtopping of an embankment system, typically at the downstream end of a site at an elevation lower than the exterior berm.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Pump</td>
      <td>Water pump infrastructure (pad, pump, enclosure) used to introduce or remove water from a MSMU or backwater lake.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Well</td>
      <td>Vertical hole drilled into the ground to access or influence groundwater movement, used to introduce or remove water from a MSMU or backwater lake.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Stoplog</td>
      <td>Water management structure that allows control of water level or flow rate into or out of MSMUs and backwater lakes by adding or removing stoplogs.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other</td>
      <td>Other method; specify in sdsFeatureDescription.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### sdsMetaDataID
References attached metadata.

### RestorFeatIDPK
Primary key used to uniquely identify the restoration feature record.

### sdsID
Identifier used to link the feature to supporting SDS (spatial data system) records or related datasets.

### mediaIDFK
Foreign key used to reference associated media (e.g., photographs, design drawings, operating plans, as-built plans) documenting the moist soil management unit.
